# Introduction

TKCat provides a [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io)
(MCP) server which lets an AI assistant
(e.g. [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code), Claude Desktop or any
other MCP client) explore and query the modeled databases (MDBs) available in
a chTKCat instance.

The assistant takes advantage of the information documented in each MDB:
the general description of the resource, the data model with
table and field comments, primary and foreign keys, and the collection members
used to integrate different MDBs.

The server is written in R and can be used in two ways:

- **Local server** (`chTKCat_mcp_server()`): the server is launched by
the MCP client on the user's computer and communicates with it through the
standard input and output (stdio transport). It connects to the chTKCat
instance, which can be local or remote.
See the [Local server](#local-server-stdio) section.
- **Remote server** (`chTKCat_mcp_http_server()`): the server runs as a
service on a remote machine, usually next to the chTKCat instance, and
remote MCP clients connect to it through HTTPS (Streamable HTTP transport).
Users don't need R nor TKCat on their computer.
See the [Remote server](#remote-server-http) section.

## Available tools

| Tool | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `list_mdbs` | List the MDBs with their title, description, version, size and access level |
| `search_tkcat` | Search MDBs, tables and fields by keyword (relies on `search_MDB_tables()` and `search_MDB_fields()`) |
| `describe_mdb` | General information, tables (with format and dimensions), relationships and collection members of an MDB |
| `describe_tables` | Detailed data model of tables: fields, R and ClickHouse types, keys, indexes, collection members |
| `preview_table` | First records of a table or of a matrix |
| `query_mdb` | Run a read-only ClickHouse SQL `SELECT` query on an MDB |
| `get_matrix_values` | Get values from a matrix table for selected rows and/or columns |
| `list_collections` | Collections of concepts (e.g. genes, conditions) and their members in the different MDBs |

In `query_mdb`, the tables of the MDB are referred to by their names in the
data model (e.g. `SELECT * FROM genes`). Tables of other MDBs can be referred
to as `` `MDB`.`table` `` to integrate several resources in the same query.

## Read-only access

The server can only read data. It cannot write, create or delete anything and
it cannot modify grants:

- The ClickHouse session is opened with the `readonly = 2` setting.
ClickHouse rejects any query modifying data, tables, databases, users or grants,
and this setting cannot be changed during the session.
- SQL statements are checked before being sent to ClickHouse: only single
`SELECT` queries (possibly starting with `WITH`) are accepted, without
`SETTINGS` nor `INTO OUTFILE` clauses and without table functions accessing
external resources (e.g. `url()`, `file()`, `s3()`, `remote()`).
- The server only accesses the MDBs readable by the ClickHouse user
used for the connection.

# Local server (stdio)

## Requirements

- R (>= 4.1) and the TKCat package (version >= 1.3.0) installed on the
computer running the MCP client:

```{r}
install.packages("TKCat")
## or the development version
devtools::install_github("patzaw/TKCat")
```

- The `Rscript` command must be available in the `PATH`
(otherwise use its full path in the configurations below,
e.g.
`C:\\Users\\user_name\\AppData\\Local\\Programs\\R\\R-4.6.1\\bin\\Rscript.exe`
on Windows).

- A chTKCat instance reachable from this computer.

## ClickHouse user

The server connects to chTKCat with the credentials provided in the
following environment variables:

| Variable | Description | Default |
|----------|-------------|---------|
| `TKCAT_HOST` | chTKCat host | `localhost` |
| `TKCAT_PORT` | chTKCat HTTP port | `9111` |
| `TKCAT_USER` | ClickHouse user | `default` |
| `TKCAT_PASSWORD` | user password | `""` |
| `TKCAT_HTTPS` | use HTTPS (`TRUE` or `FALSE`) | `FALSE` |

The `default` user gives access to the public MDBs only.
To access private MDBs, it is recommended to use a dedicated user
without any admin right, created by a chTKCat administrator:

```{r}
library(TKCat)
k <- chTKCat(host = "localhost", port = 9111, user = "admin_user")
create_chTKCat_user(k, login = "mcp_user", contact = NA, admin = FALSE)
## Give access to a private MDB
add_chMDB_user(k, mdb = "Private_MDB", login = "mcp_user", admin = FALSE)
```

## Checking the server

The following command, run in a terminal, starts the server.
It should write a message such as `chTKCat MCP server ready` and then wait
for MCP requests on its standard input (stop it with Ctrl+C).

```{bash}
TKCAT_HOST=localhost TKCAT_PORT=9111 TKCAT_USER=default \
   Rscript -e "TKCat::chTKCat_mcp_server()"
```

The [MCP Inspector](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/tools/inspector)
can be used to try the tools interactively (requires Node.js):

```{bash}
npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector \
   -e TKCAT_HOST=localhost -e TKCAT_PORT=9111 \
   -- Rscript -e "TKCat::chTKCat_mcp_server()"
```

## Configuring an MCP client

### Claude Code

Register the server with the `claude mcp add` command
(`--scope user` makes it available in all your projects):

```{bash}
claude mcp add tkcat --scope user \
   -e TKCAT_HOST=localhost -e TKCAT_PORT=9111 \
   -e TKCAT_USER=mcp_user -e TKCAT_PASSWORD=xxxxxx \
   -- Rscript -e "TKCat::chTKCat_mcp_server()"
```

Check that the server is connected with `claude mcp list` or with the
`/mcp` command within Claude Code.

To share the configuration with the other members of a project,
a `.mcp.json` file can be added at the root of the project.
Credentials should not be written in this file: they can be taken from
the environment of each user with the `${VARIABLE}` syntax.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "tkcat": {
      "command": "Rscript",
      "args": ["-e", "TKCat::chTKCat_mcp_server()"],
      "env": {
        "TKCAT_HOST": "tkcat.example.com",
        "TKCAT_PORT": "9111",
        "TKCAT_USER": "${TKCAT_USER}",
        "TKCAT_PASSWORD": "${TKCAT_PASSWORD}"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Claude Desktop

Add the server in the `claude_desktop_config.json` file
(Settings > Developer > Edit Config) and restart Claude Desktop:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "tkcat": {
      "command": "Rscript",
      "args": ["-e", "TKCat::chTKCat_mcp_server()"],
      "env": {
        "TKCAT_HOST": "localhost",
        "TKCAT_PORT": "9111",
        "TKCAT_USER": "mcp_user",
        "TKCAT_PASSWORD": "xxxxxx"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Other MCP clients

Any MCP client supporting the stdio transport can use the server with
the same command (`Rscript`), arguments
(`-e "TKCat::chTKCat_mcp_server()"`) and environment variables.

## Server parameters

The `chTKCat_mcp_server()` function has additional parameters
which can be set in the R expression given to `Rscript`:

- `maxRows`: maximum number of rows returned by a query (default: 1000).
- `maxChars`: maximum number of characters returned by a tool call
(default: 60000). Longer outputs are truncated.
- `maxExecutionTime`: maximum execution time of a query in seconds
(default: 300).

For example:

```{bash}
Rscript -e "TKCat::chTKCat_mcp_server(maxRows = 500, maxExecutionTime = 60)"
```

# Remote server (HTTP)

## Architecture

The remote server is run as a service on a machine which can reach the
chTKCat instance (usually the same machine). A reverse proxy (nginx)
provides HTTPS and forwards the requests to one or several instances of the
R server listening on the local interface only:

```
MCP client  --HTTPS-->  nginx (:443)  --HTTP-->  R MCP server(s) (127.0.0.1:8801, 8802...)  --HTTP-->  chTKCat (ClickHouse :9111)
```

- **Authentication.** Users authenticate with their own chTKCat credentials
sent in an HTTP Basic `Authorization` header. The credentials are checked by
ClickHouse and each user only accesses the MDBs they are allowed to read.
The server does not store any credential on disk.
- **Stateless.** The server does not create MCP sessions and answers each
request with a single JSON response. Several instances can thus run in
parallel behind nginx: since R processes one request at a time, running
several instances avoids a long query blocking the other users.
- **Read-only.** The same tools and the same read-only protections as for the
local server are applied to each user connection.

## Running the server

On the server machine, install R and TKCat in a site library (available to
the user running the service). Then the server can be started with:

```{bash}
TKCAT_HOST=localhost TKCAT_PORT=9111 TKCAT_MCP_PORT=8801 \
   Rscript -e "TKCat::chTKCat_mcp_http_server()"
```

The main parameters of `chTKCat_mcp_http_server()` are the following
(see `?chTKCat_mcp_http_server` for the complete list):

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|-----------|-------------|---------|
| `mcpHost` | Listening address | `TKCAT_MCP_HOST` or `127.0.0.1` |
| `mcpPort` | Listening port | `TKCAT_MCP_PORT` or `8800` |
| `mcpPath` | Path of the MCP endpoint | `/mcp` |
| `host`, `port`, `https` | chTKCat connection | `TKCAT_HOST`, `TKCAT_PORT`, `TKCAT_HTTPS` |
| `anonymousUser` | ClickHouse user used for requests without credentials (e.g. `"default"` to give access to public MDBs without authentication) | `TKCAT_MCP_ANONYMOUS_USER` or `NA` (authentication required) |
| `anonymousPassword` | Password of `anonymousUser` | `TKCAT_MCP_ANONYMOUS_PASSWORD` or `""` |
| `allowedOrigins` | Accepted values of the `Origin` header (only sent by web browsers) | `NULL` (requests with an `Origin` header are rejected) |
| `maxRows`, `maxChars`, `maxExecutionTime` | Same as for the local server | `1000`, `60000`, `300` |
| `cacheTime` | Seconds during which user connections and data models are kept in memory | `3600` |

Keep the default `mcpHost = "127.0.0.1"` when the server is behind nginx on
the same machine: the R server does not provide HTTPS and must not be directly
reachable from the network.

Tool calls are logged on the standard error output with the time, the client
address, the user and the name of the tool:

```
2026-10-10 14:46:51 - 10.1.2.3 - jdoe - query_mdb
```

## Running the server as a systemd service

The following systemd template unit, saved as
`/etc/systemd/system/tkcat-mcp@.service`, runs an instance of the server
on the port given as instance name. It is run by a dedicated system user
(`tkcat-mcp`) without any privilege.

```ini
[Unit]
Description=chTKCat MCP server (port %i)
After=network-online.target
Wants=network-online.target

[Service]
User=tkcat-mcp
Group=tkcat-mcp
Environment=TKCAT_HOST=localhost
Environment=TKCAT_PORT=9111
Environment=TKCAT_MCP_HOST=127.0.0.1
Environment=TKCAT_MCP_PORT=%i
EnvironmentFile=-/etc/tkcat-mcp.env
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/Rscript -e "TKCat::chTKCat_mcp_http_server()"
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=5
NoNewPrivileges=true
PrivateTmp=true
ProtectSystem=strict
ProtectHome=read-only

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

Anonymous access is configured in the optional `/etc/tkcat-mcp.env` file
(the leading `-` in `EnvironmentFile=-` makes it optional: without this
file, authentication is required for all the requests).
This file is read by systemd before dropping privileges: it can thus be
readable by root only, which keeps the password out of the command line and
out of the files readable by the `tkcat-mcp` user.

```ini
TKCAT_MCP_ANONYMOUS_USER=techuser
TKCAT_MCP_ANONYMOUS_PASSWORD=techuser_password
```

Create the system user, protect the environment file and start, for example,
4 instances:

```{bash}
sudo useradd --system --no-create-home --shell /usr/sbin/nologin tkcat-mcp
sudo chown root:root /etc/tkcat-mcp.env
sudo chmod 600 /etc/tkcat-mcp.env
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now tkcat-mcp@8801 tkcat-mcp@8802 tkcat-mcp@8803 tkcat-mcp@8804
## Logs
sudo journalctl -u 'tkcat-mcp@*' -f
```

## nginx configuration

The following configuration, saved for example as
`/etc/nginx/conf.d/tkcat-mcp.conf`, provides HTTPS, distributes the requests
among the server instances and limits the request rate by client
(which also slows down password guessing attempts).
Replace `tkcat.example.com` and the certificate paths with your own values.

```nginx
limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=tkcat_mcp:10m rate=5r/s;

## R MCP server instances (see the systemd service above)
upstream tkcat_mcp_inst {
    least_conn;
    server 127.0.0.1:8801;
    server 127.0.0.1:8802;
    server 127.0.0.1:8803;
    server 127.0.0.1:8804;
    keepalive 8;
}

## Other config commands
## ...

server {

    ## Other config commands
    ## ...
    
    ## TKCat MCP server
    location = /tkcat_mcp {
        limit_req zone=tkcat_mcp burst=20 nodelay;
        client_max_body_size 1m;

        proxy_pass http://tkcat_mcp_inst/mcp;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Connection "";
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        ## Client address used in the logs of the R server
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $remote_addr;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;

        ## Must be longer than the maxExecutionTime of the R server
        proxy_read_timeout 330s;
        proxy_send_timeout 330s;
        proxy_buffering off;
    }

    ## ...
}
```

Check and reload the configuration:

```{bash}
sudo nginx -t && sudo systemctl reload nginx
```

The `Authorization` header is forwarded by nginx without modification.
Do not enable nginx access logs with request bodies or headers:
they would record the credentials and the queries of the users.

## Checking the server

The server can be checked with `curl` (`-u` provides the credentials
in a Basic `Authorization` header):

```{bash}
curl -u jdoe:xxxxxx https://tkcat.example.com/tkcat_mcp \
   -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
   -H "Accept: application/json, text/event-stream" \
   -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"list_mdbs","arguments":{}}}'
```

The server answers with:

- **200** and a JSON-RPC response for MCP requests;
- **202** for notifications;
- **401** if the credentials are missing or wrong;
- **403** for requests with a non-allowed `Origin` header;
- **405** for methods other than POST (no server-sent event stream);
- **502** if the chTKCat instance cannot be reached.

## Configuring remote MCP clients

Users provide their chTKCat credentials as the Base64 encoding of
`user:password`, which can be computed in a terminal or in R:

```{bash}
printf '%s' 'jdoe:xxxxxx' | base64
```

```{r}
jsonlite::base64_enc("jdoe:xxxxxx")
```

### Claude Code

```{bash}
claude mcp add tkcat --scope user --transport http \
   https://tkcat.example.com/tkcat_mcp \
   --header "Authorization: Basic amRvZTp4eHh4eHg="
```

In a project `.mcp.json` file shared with other users, the credentials
can be taken from the environment of each user (here from a `TKCAT_MCP_AUTH`
environment variable with the Base64 value):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "tkcat": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://tkcat.example.com/tkcat_mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Basic ${TKCAT_MCP_AUTH}"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Other MCP clients

Any MCP client supporting the Streamable HTTP transport and custom headers can
connect to `https://tkcat.example.com/tkcat_mcp` with the `Authorization` header
described above.

Clients supporting only the stdio transport (e.g. Claude Desktop with a local
configuration file) can use a bridge such as
[mcp-remote](https://www.npmjs.com/package/mcp-remote) (requires Node.js;
check that third-party tools are allowed by your organization):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "tkcat": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "mcp-remote", "https://tkcat.example.com/tkcat_mcp",
        "--header", "Authorization:${TKCAT_MCP_AUTH}"
      ],
      "env": {
        "NODE_OPTIONS": "--use-system-ca"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The `NODE_OPTIONS` environment variable set to `--use-system-ca` tells
Node.js to trust the certificate authorities (CA) installed in the
operating system certificate store. By default, Node.js only relies on its
own bundled list of public CAs. Thus, if the certificate of the nginx server
is signed by an internal CA of your organization (or if the HTTPS traffic is
inspected by a corporate proxy), the connection fails with errors such as
`unable to get local issuer certificate` or
`self-signed certificate in certificate chain`.
This option requires a recent version of Node.js (>= 22.15).
With older versions, the `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` environment variable can be
set instead, with the path to a PEM file containing the internal CA
certificate(s). The `env` entry can be removed if the server certificate is
signed by a public CA.

Connectors added in the web interface of claude.ai are connected from
Anthropic's cloud: they would require the server to be reachable from the
internet and to support OAuth authentication, which is not provided by
this server.

# Usage

Once the server is configured, questions can be asked in natural language.
For example:

- *Which resources provide information about gene expression in tissues?*
- *What is the data model of the GTEx MDB?*
- *In which tissues is the SCN1A gene the most expressed according to GTEx?*
- *Which MDBs can be integrated with HGNC through gene identifiers?*

The assistant generally follows this workflow:

1. It identifies relevant MDBs with `list_mdbs` and `search_tkcat`.
2. It reads the description and the data model of these MDBs with
`describe_mdb` and `describe_tables`.
3. It looks at a few records with `preview_table`.
4. It answers the question with `query_mdb` or `get_matrix_values`,
possibly combining several MDBs thanks to the collection members
(`list_collections`).

# Security considerations

- Data returned by the tools are sent to the AI assistant.
Only configure the server with a user accessing MDBs whose content can be
shared with the AI service you are using, according to your organization's
policies.
- The password is stored in plain text in the configuration of the MCP client
(environment variables or Base64-encoded `Authorization` header, which is
**not** encrypted): use a dedicated user with read-only access to the relevant
MDBs only.
- Use HTTPS (`TKCAT_HTTPS=TRUE`) when connecting to a remote chTKCat instance.
- With the remote server:
    - always use HTTPS between the clients and nginx: Basic credentials are
    sent in clear text otherwise;
    - keep the R server listening on the local interface (`127.0.0.1`) and
    expose it only through nginx;
    - restrict the access to the internal network when possible and
    consult your security team before exposing the service;
    - setting `anonymousUser` gives access to the corresponding MDBs to anyone
    reaching the server.
- Messages and errors are written on the standard error output, which is
generally available in the logs of the MCP client (local server) or in the
service logs (remote server).
